content.title: About
content.content: The cookie, chocolate chip sandwich consists of two soft cookies with a layer of buttery cream in between, topped with chocolate chip pieces. It combines a crisp cookie texture with a smooth, sweet cream and the distinctive aroma of chocolate.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The first sandwich‑cookie recipe appeared in the United States in the 1970s.
Original recipes use dark chocolate chips with at least 55 % cocoa content.
The cookies are often packaged in single‑serve packs to keep the cream fresh.
In some markets a pinch of sea salt is added to the cream to enhance flavor.

items.title: Energy source
items.content: Carbohydrates from the cookies and fats from the cream provide a quick boost of energy.

items.title: Contains antioxidants
items.content: Dark chocolate chips are rich in flavonoids, which help combat free radicals.

items.title: Calcium from dairy
items.content: The buttery cream, made with milk, contributes to daily calcium intake.

items.title: Milk and gluten allergy
items.content: The product contains wheat flour and dairy ingredients, which may trigger reactions in sensitive individuals.

items.title: High sugar content
items.content: The sweet cream and chocolate chips make the snack calorie‑dense; moderate consumption is advised for those monitoring blood sugar.

items.title: Trans fats
items.content: Some commercial versions use partially hydrogenated oils; choose products labeled trans‑fat free.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Enjoy the sandwich as a standalone snack, add it to lunch boxes, or crumble it over ice cream or yogurt for a dessert topping.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store in an airtight container in a cool, dry place. For longer shelf life keep refrigerated to maintain cream freshness. Discard if the product develops off‑odors or visible mold.
